no_finding_evidence.area: Canonical shared ownership and distribution replication
no_finding_evidence.result: Canonical shared inputs are explicitly listed and path-allowlisted before assembly (distribution.mjs:286-363); each selected skill receives only its declared shared asset set (159-167, 656-672). Host-rendered common resources get refreshed manual and context digests (538-617, 625-632), and runtime verification checks manual, test-discipline, product-protocol and context digests (verify-engineering-manual.mjs:267-359). No reportable duplicated ownership or redundant semantic re-audit was established.

Renderer has closed host names and host-specific substitutions, rejects unknown/unresolved tokens, removes Codex invocation frontmatter when rendering Codex, and emits Codex sidecars only for canonical/Codex outputs (distribution.mjs:43-101,232-284,640-672). The current three host roots are present. A bounded read-only SHA-256 comparison of five relevant canonical shared reference paths against existing host copies found ten existing copies: eight exact matches and two Codex/Claude workflow-state-access mismatches; source lines 3 and 5 of the canonical file contain declared host template tokens, consistent with expected host rendering, while the Harness copy matched the canonical bytes. This was not a full rendered-output or all-file fidelity proof. Existing test definitions explicitly cover Harness leakage and host-rendered digest behavior (deepseek-export.test.mjs:27-64,147-168).
evidence: Read-only SHA-256 comparison: 10 existing reference copies; 8 exact raw matches; 2 expected host-template candidates; no Harness mismatch among those paths.

no_finding_evidence.result: Generation validates sources, constructs expected outputs, then either compares without writes or replaces outputs (generate.mjs:39-79). Exact byte comparison also checks complete managed path sets and unsafe paths (distribution.mjs:810-864). Publication stages a complete expected tree, preflights targets, preserves backups, verifies after publication, and reverses operations on failure while preserving sibling exports (distribution.mjs:962-1061). Existing tests define check/tamper/rollback/sibling-preservation and unsafe-symlink cases (deepseek-export.test.mjs:170-200); these are source-inspected expectations, not executed results. No missing recovery optimization was confirmed.

Catalog validation pins the exact 17-skill inventory, order, closed fields, dependencies and explicit-only host policies (catalog.mjs:83-163,166-234); the skill parser rejects invalid UTF-8, unsupported frontmatter, NUL/CRLF and mismatched policies while applying a 240-code-point description limit and 4096-byte document limit (skill-document.mjs:30-55,97-219). Source validation and generated expected-document construction revalidate at the respective boundaries (validate.mjs:66-157; distribution.mjs:366-393,633-647). Static tests define exact size-boundary and host packaging/private-path assertions (skill-document.test.mjs:77-96; packaging.test.mjs:402-450,650-680). No overall package size cap or measured size regression was established in inspected code.

limitations: No scenario MCP tool was needed: workflow-managed catalog/experience/manifest YAML and live scenario state were not accessed or parsed. Only static JSON collection metadata was inspected.
No generation/check command, audited skill, build, pack/install/publish operation, or test was executed; safety constraints require source-and-test inspection only.

The comparison covered five selected shared reference paths and the existence/inventory of three host roots, not every generated file or a complete all-host rendered-byte comparison. Two raw Codex/Claude differences were not treated as leaks because canonical text contains declared host variables; the corresponding full renderer output was not generated or independently normalized.
